summary.text: A 35-year-old man with no significant past medical history was found unconscious in a closed room containing a burned-out charcoal brazier on December 24, 2024. After oxygen by face mask he reached the emergency department with a heart rate of 115 beats/min, respiratory rate 30 breaths/min, oxygen saturation 91% and Glasgow Coma Scale E2V2M5. Carboxyhemoglobin was 23%, and CT showed reduced density in the bilateral globus pallidus.

Emergency hyperbaric oxygen therapy was started at 0.25 MPa for 60 minutes. During decompression he suddenly developed dyspnea, severe cough and frothy sputum, and on ward admission had a heart rate of 135 beats/min, oxygen saturation 82% and coarse crackles, wheezing and crepitus. APE with subcutaneous emphysema was indicated; endotracheal intubation, mechanical ventilation, diuretics, corticosteroids and bronchodilators followed. Follow-up CT showed pulmonary exudation, mediastinal and subcutaneous emphysema and a small bilateral pneumothorax.

His condition gradually stabilized after active treatment and the endotracheal tube was removed after 48 hours. A repeat CT showed significant improvement in pulmonary edema with complete resolution of the subcutaneous, mediastinal and subpleural gases. He was transferred to Rehabilitation Medicine, discharged in a recovered state 10 days later, and was asymptomatic at the 3-month follow-up.
